targetTest: journal: a failed sync rejects the commit and leaves the world untouched
expected: After a sync that fails (or a write that stops mid-record) the journal reports TornTail at the verified prefix with the unacknowledged byte count and lastGoodSeq, and a further submit is refused JournalNotClean instead of writing a second @commit N on top of unconfirmed bytes; lastGoodSeq names the last verified commit in every status; a bad byte count in a commit head line reports the record's head-line offset
actual: 4 of 9 journal cases fail on assertions: the journal stays Ok after an unacknowledged append and accepts the next submit; lastGoodSeq is 0 at every Ok boundary of the truncation sweep; a flipped count digit in commit 2 reports offset 974 (inside commit 3). The 5 passing cases pin tracer behavior that already existed (write/sync order, refusal while torn/corrupt, flock, header-only fresh world, open never modifies the file).
